decisions.reason: As a core bread product that remained visible after launch and fits the bakery’s established production and sales routines, it is inexpensive to keep while there is no clear evidence that its value has failed to materialize.

The sweet pastry is somewhat more assortment-sensitive than staple bread, but it still lies close to the firm’s core capabilities and there is too little negative information to justify abandoning the option.
This farmhouse bread is a closely related extension of the firm’s main bread business, so the option value of continuing it remains favorable given low retention costs and no observed poor result.

Although seasonal and more niche, the poppy seed Christmas stollen has an award signal and likely uses existing festive production capabilities, so it is worth retaining unless later sales clearly disappoint.
The premium Christmas stollen shows a positive quality signal from its gold award and is likely a strong seasonal flagship, making continued market presence the higher-value choice.
